contributions.statement: Do not vet third-party SKILL.md bundles with SAST/SCA, rule-based skill scanners or generic prompt-injection detectors: attacks that split harmful intent between skill instructions and innocuous helper scripts were detected in at most 17% of cases.
contributions.evidence: §VI-B Table IV: skill-security-scan 2-8%, Snyk Agent Scan 9-17%, held-out SkillScan 0-1.3%; LLM-Guard 4.0%, PIGuard 17.1%. Mutations were refined against these scanners (adaptive lower bound, §IV-C).

contributions.statement: If skills are shared across agent hosts, use an LLM-based install-time review (frontier or a local distilled model) plus human approval, since LLM reviewers caught roughly 80-88% of these attacks but flagged about 8% of clean skills.
contributions.evidence: §VI-D Fig. 6 (GPT-5.4 86.8%, distilled 7B 88.2%, in-distribution for the student); §VI-E Table VII FPR 8.0% on 100 clean ClawHub skills; App. B-B precision 60.9%.

reason: The only KB paper measuring malicious-skill detection; it shows that existing scanners miss cross-modal skill attacks, which matters for a team sharing skills across hosts.
